newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger president to free detained opponents.
newsitem.headline: Niger president to free detained opponents.

text.p: Niger's President, Ibrahim Bare Mainassara, has announced he will release detained opponents to create the conditions for the formation of a broad-based government and end social and political unrest.

Mainassara's announcement, in a message to the nation broadcast by state television late on Thursday, said reconciliation was the only way the arid West African nation would win the battle against poverty.
"I have decided, in response to calls for pardon and reconciliation, to free all my compatriots arrested during the events of January 11," he said.
Dozens of opposition activists, including Niger's three main opposition leaders, were arrested after a banned January 11 opposition protest to demand broader access to state media.

They accuse Mainassara of rigging a July presidential election to consolidate his rule after staging a coup a year ago. Mahamane Ousmane, the civilian president Mainassara ousted, was among those detained.

It was not immediately clear when the detainees would be released but Mainassara, whose supporters easily won November parliamentary elections boycotted by the opposition, said his aim was to broaden the government.

"As president of all Niger citizens I have decided to place myself above the (political) parties to create conditions favourable to the creation of a broadly based government," he said. "It is through joining together and concorde that the people of Niger will win the struggle against poverty."

The arrests triggered opposition protests and criticism from abroad. Former colonial power France and the United States, which has denounced Mainassara's election victory as fraudulent, urged their release.
The three opposition leaders were being investigated for threatening state security.
